title: Cluster declaration versus exposed state
summary: The matching ZHA quirk retains a DoorLock cluster. Zigbee2MQTT declares separate command/state and actual-state fields. These artifacts alone do not establish equal UI behavior or a complete cross-platform mapping.

observations.claim: YRD210PBDB220TSLL includes DoorLock in its signature and replacement input clusters. The quirk itself does not define the downstream HA lock entity's states.
conditions: Endpoint and complete cluster signature must match.
Cluster presence is not whole-platform exposure or hardware success.

observations.claim: The shared e.lock() constructor declares state as LOCK/UNLOCK with state/set/get access, and lock_state as not_fully_locked/locked/unlocked with state-only access.
conditions: Model-only matcher; no explicit manufacturer constraint in this definition.
Exposed metadata is not a firmware capability test or confirmation that all state values occur.

limitations: Human-authored candidate observations; no independent EdgeLoom review or physical-device test.
Sources are pinned snapshots, not a claim about the currently installed integration, coordinator or firmware.
Relationship labels are curator interpretations, not computed semantic equivalence. Conflicting observations must remain visible.
No SDF correspondence is added for this Zigbee case; lack of a catalog binding is not a limitation of SDF.
Commands, observations and partially locked state must not be collapsed into a single binary semantic binding.
